objective: Improve geometric-mean WHATWG URL parse, href serialize/update, and URLSearchParams parse/serialize throughput using the pinned upstream benchmark/url harness. All parallel/test-url* and parallel/test-whatwg-url* tests, byte-exact serialized outputs, and peak heap/RSS no greater than the measured baseline plus 2% are hard gates. Only src/node_url.cc, src/node_url.h, lib/internal/url.js, deps/ada/ada.cpp, deps/ada/ada.h, and deps/ada/ada_c.h are mutable.

meta.provenance: nodejs/node at exact revision 9df0e9b4d4a5be5ce7506fae44acb6667bb68d6b; current-head terminal capsule with no reference patch; baseline commit is a synthetic sealed-store commit layering the trusted evaluator glue over the pinned upstream WHATWG URL surface; terminal holdout assets and all diagnostic measurements remain capsule-local and were never exposed to an optimizer; trusted parent-side marginal wall-clock baseline stability samples [2506995.963308928, 2478857.8243704624, 2472401.336947227] give qBase=2486085.041542206 and sample sigma=18394.878208677652; qReference=qBase+max(5*sigma,0.05*abs(qBase-qFail))=2610389.293619316; independently authored URLSearchParams serialization caching passes all gates and moves q

measurement.platform: linux/arm64 Docker Desktop on Apple M3 Max; final recalibration required on the frozen GCE Linux host
measurement.q: geometric mean ops/sec across 16 frozen upstream benchmark/url cells per split; throughput is derived by the trusted parent evaluator from the marginal wall-clock between the fastest-of-2 base-scale and fastest-of-2 8x-scale runs of each protected upstream cell (trimmed sampling rejects host-contention outliers), never from candidate-emitted output

exploitReview.protectedPathEscape: the broker protects evaluator, build, benchmark, test, fixture, and toolchain paths; the evaluator byte-hashes every non-mutable candidate file that appears in the workspace against the trusted baseline and rejects additions, mismatches, symlinks, and repository metadata, while intentionally-hidden protected files are simply absent from the sanitized workspace
exploitReview.benchmarkSpecialCasing: train and validation choose disjoint holdout benchmark/common URL and SearchParams identities; the shortcut diagnostic accelerates recognized train inputs but is slowed and rejected in ordering on unseen validation inputs
exploitReview.fixtureFingerprinting: both terminal splits are holdout-visible only to the trusted terminal diagnostic path; workload JSON is staged root-only and only validated benchmark arguments are passed to unprivileged processes
exploitReview.outputFabrication: a protected exact-output worker independently constructs real URL and URLSearchParams objects and byte-compares href and form serialization against sealed expected outputs before scoring; benchmark throughput is computed by the trusted parent from its own monotonic wall-clock across base and 8x workload scales with fastest-of-2 trimmed sampling per scale, so candidate-controlled stdout, IPC, or in-process timers never set the score, and any cell whose marginal wall-clock is not strictly above the resolution floor is rejected outright instead of earning a bounded floor rate
exploitReview.timerTampering: the trusted parent evaluator measures benchmark wall-clock outside every candidate-linked process; the protected NODE_OPTIONS memory probe additionally pins process.hrtime before the upstream harness loads candidate URL code, and candidate-reported rates serve only as structural completion markers
exploitReview.testShortCircuit: each parallel URL test additionally runs under a protected sentinel preload bound to a parent-held pipe pair: the nonce is delivered over a parent-written pipe drained at preload time (never via the environment) and the completion receipt returns over a pipe whose read end only the trusted worker holds, is required to match byte-exactly, and fires only after the event loop drains naturally with exit code zero, checked against a frozen per-file inventory, so candidate code that prints a marker or terminates a test child early fails the gate instead of hiding assertion bodies
exploitReview.buildScriptMutation: configuration, Ninja graph, evaluator, worker, benchmark sources, tests, and toolchain lock are protected; only six implementation files are copied into a fresh image-backed build volume
exploitReview.deadCodeBenchmarkBypass: the protected upstream scripts retain live result values and benchmark the same URL and URLSearchParams entry points covered by the exact-output gate and upstream parallel tests
